we developed a Bayesian active-learning algorithm that accurately assesses children’s word-reading abilities, and that we integrated it into a robot that is able to tutor children’s reading skills in a personalized manner.

(a) we developed a Bayesian active-learning algorithm that continuously and accurately assesses a child's word-reading skills; (b) we implemented the algorithm in a social robot that is portrayed as a child and used to assess the child's reading skills; (c) we show that implementing the algorithm results in an age-and initial reading skill-independent tutoring; and (d) we show that the child’s perception of what the robot knows is comparable to the robot’s knowledge and age-dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an integrated system that enables continuous assessment of the child, personalization of the tutoring interaction to the child, and the development of a child-specific representation of the robot’s skills, which may enable a child-specific tutoring interaction.
developing and evaluating a tutoring system that is effective for children’s learning of a new skill and that is also effective for the robot’s learning of new knowledge.
developing an integrated system for assessing and tutoring children’s reading skills. We show that such a system is feasible and can lead to improved learning outcomes.
